title: Direct provider SDK vs AI framework
problem: You need to call a model from an app and wonder whether to adopt LangChain/LlamaIndex/etc. first.
tradeOffs: Frameworks accelerate connectors; direct SDKs keep control and clearer data flow.
complexity: Low for direct SDK; medium+ for frameworks.
lockIn: Framework abstractions and vendor-specific helpers can increase switching cost.
security: Either path needs output validation and secret hygiene; frameworks can hide tool surfaces.
cost: Framework OSS is free; complexity cost dominates early.
exampleScenarios: Single structured extraction call → direct SDK
Many retrievers/tools evolving weekly → framework may help

title: LangChain vs LangGraph
problem: Choosing between chains/composables and stateful graph orchestration.
tradeOffs: LangChain helps compose; LangGraph models stateful agent graphs.
lockIn: Graph state shapes become core architecture.
security: Stateful agents amplify excessive agency risks.

title: LangChain vs LlamaIndex
problem: Picking a data/RAG-centric vs general orchestration framework.
tradeOffs: LlamaIndex strong on data indexes; LangChain broad integrations.

title: Vercel AI SDK vs direct SDK
problem: TypeScript app needs streaming chat UI.
tradeOffs: AI SDK speeds UI patterns; direct SDK maximizes control.
complexity: AI SDK lower for Next.js chat.
cost: SDK free; tokens billed by provider.

title: pgvector vs dedicated vector database
problem: Where to store embeddings for RAG.
tradeOffs: pgvector co-locates with SQL; dedicated engines optimize ANN ops.
complexity: pgvector lower if Postgres already owned.
lockIn: Managed vector vendors vs Postgres extension.
security: Row-level security vs namespace isolation models.
cost: Often cheaper to start on Postgres; scale may shift economics.

title: Hosted vs local/open model
problem: Privacy, cost, and quality trade-offs for inference.
tradeOffs: Hosted quality/ops ease vs local control/privacy.
security: Data leaves boundary on hosted; local still needs output controls.
exampleScenarios: Peak SaaS traffic → hosted or vLLM

title: RAG vs fine-tuning
tradeOffs: RAG grounds facts; fine-tune shapes behavior—not a substitute for retrieval of changing docs.
security: Training data rights; retrieval poisoning for RAG.
exampleScenarios: Policy PDFs that change weekly → RAG
Consistent extraction style → maybe light tune + schemas

title: Deterministic workflow vs agent
problem: When to let a model choose tools dynamically.
tradeOffs: Deterministic workflows are testable; agents handle open-ended tasks with higher variance.
security: Excessive agency risk rises with agents.
exampleScenarios: Ops triage with many tools → constrained agent

title: LangGraph vs ordinary application workflow
problem: Whether graph agent framework beats explicit app code.
tradeOffs: App workflows are transparent; LangGraph helps complex agent graphs.
security: Same tool permission rules either way.
exampleScenarios: CRUD + one model call → app workflow

title: Ollama vs vLLM
tradeOffs: Ollama great for local DX; vLLM targets high-throughput serving.
security: Both need API auth when exposed.

title: MCP vs custom integrations
problem: Standardize tool access vs bespoke adapters.
tradeOffs: MCP standardizes; custom may be thinner for one integration.
security: Tool permission model critical either way.
exampleScenarios: One internal HTTP tool → custom may suffice

title: Cursor vs other coding agents by use case
problem: Choosing an AI coding environment for repo work.
tradeOffs: Cursor emphasizes Agent + rules/skills/MCP; others optimize IDE completion or CLI loops.
exampleScenarios: Unfamiliar repo change with rules → Cursor
Inline completion in JetBrains → Copilot-like tools
